The Gold Room within the [Mount Washington Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Washington_Hotel "Mount Washington Hotel"), where the [Bretton Woods Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bretton_Woods_Conference "Bretton Woods Conference") attendees signed the agreements creating the IMF and [World Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank "World Bank") [![Image 22](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Articles_of_Agreement_of_the_International_Monetary_Fund.jpg/250px-Articles_of_Agreement_of_the_International_Monetary_Fund.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Articles_of_Agreement_of_the_International_Monetary_Fund.jpg) First page of the Articles of Agreement of the International Monetary Fund, 1 March 1946, Finnish Ministry of Foreign Affairs archives The IMF was originally laid out as a part of the [Bretton Woods system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bretton_Woods_system "Bretton Woods system") exchange agreement in the year 1944.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-Jensen,_pp_194-210-18) During the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression"), countries sharply raised barriers to trade in an attempt to improve their failing economies. This led to the [devaluation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devaluation "Devaluation") of national currencies and a decline in world trade.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-CoopAndRecon-19) This breakdown in international monetary cooperation created a need for oversight. The representatives of 45 governments met at the [Bretton Woods Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bretton_Woods_Conference "Bretton Woods Conference") in the Mount Washington Hotel in [Bretton Woods, New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bretton_Woods,_New_Hampshire "Bretton Woods, New Hampshire"), in the United States, to discuss a framework for postwar international economic cooperation and how to rebuild Europe.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-20) There were two views on the role the IMF should assume as a global economic institution. American delegate [Harry Dexter White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Dexter_White "Harry Dexter White") foresaw an IMF that functioned more like a bank, making sure that borrowing states could repay their debts on time.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-auto-21) Most of White's plan was incorporated into the final acts adopted at Bretton Woods. British economist [John Maynard Keynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Maynard_Keynes "John Maynard Keynes"), on the other hand, imagined that the IMF would be a cooperative fund upon which member states could draw to maintain economic activity and employment through periodic crises. This view suggested an IMF that helped governments and act as the United States government had during the New Deal to [the great depression of the 1930s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-auto-21) The agreement at Bretton Woods implied that both the IMF and the World Bank would be headquartered in the United States. US Treasury Secretary [Henry Morgenthau Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Morgenthau_Jr. "Henry Morgenthau Jr.") intended them to be located in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), but his successor [Fred M. Vinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_M._Vinson "Fred M. Vinson") unilaterally decided that they would be in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") instead, noting that "the institutions would be fatally prejudiced in American opinion if they were placed in New York, since they would then come under the taint of 'international finance'".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-22):151 The IMF formally came into existence on 27 December 1945, when the first 29 countries [ratified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratified "Ratified") its Articles of Agreement.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-23) By the end of 1946 the IMF had grown to 39 members.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-Vries86-24) On 1 March 1947, the IMF began its financial operations,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-25) and on 8 May France became the first country to borrow from it.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-Vries86-24) The IMF was one of the key organizations of the international economic system; its design allowed the system to balance the rebuilding of international capitalism with the maximization of national economic sovereignty and human welfare, also known as [embedded liberalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embedded_liberalism "Embedded liberalism").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-chorev-26) The IMF's influence in the global economy steadily increased as it accumulated more members. Its membership began to expand in the late 1950s and during the 1960s as many African countries became independent and applied for membership. But the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War") limited the Fund's membership, with most countries in the Soviet sphere of influence not joining until 1970s and 1980s.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-CoopAndRecon-19)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-IMF-C6-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-28) The Bretton Woods exchange rate system prevailed until 1971 when the United States government suspended the convertibility of the US$ (and dollar reserves held by other governments) into gold. This is known as the [Nixon Shock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nixon_Shock "Nixon Shock").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-CoopAndRecon-19) The changes to the IMF articles of agreement reflecting these changes were ratified in 1976 by the [Jamaica Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_Accords "Jamaica Accords"). Later in the 1970s, large commercial banks began lending to states because they were awash in cash deposited by oil exporters. The lending of the so-called money center banks led to the IMF changing its role in the 1980s after a world recession provoked a crisis that brought the IMF back into global financial governance.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-29) In the mid-1980s, the IMF shifted its narrow focus from currency stabilization to a broader focus of promoting market-liberalizing reforms through structural adjustment programs.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-:1-30) This shift occurred without a formal renegotiation of the organization's charter or operational guidelines.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-:1-30) The [Ronald Reagan administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Ronald_Reagan "Presidency of Ronald Reagan"), in particular Treasury Secretary [James Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Baker "James Baker"), his assistant secretary [David Mulford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_C._Mulford "David C. Mulford") and deputy assistant secretary [Charles Dallara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Dallara "Charles Dallara"), pressured the IMF to attach market-liberal reforms to the organization's conditional loans.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-:1-30) During the 20th century, the IMF shifted its position on capital controls. Whereas the IMF permitted capital controls at its founding and throughout the 1970s, IMF staff increasingly favored free capital movement from 1980s onwards. This shift happened in the aftermath of an emerging consensus in economics on the desirability of free capital movement, retirement of IMF staff hired in the 1940s and 1950s, and the recruitment of staff exposed to new thinking in economics. Following the exigencies of the governments of the richest companies, the IMF, permitted countries in crisis to borrow in order to avoid default on their repayments. Caught in the debt's downward spiral, developing countries soon had no other recourse than to take on new debt in order to repay the old debt. Before providing them with new loans, at higher interest rates, future leaders asked the IMF, to intervene with the guarantee of ulterior reimbursement, asking for a signed agreement with the said countries. The IMF thus agreed to restart the flow of the 'finance pump' on condition that the concerned countries first use this money to reimburse banks and other private lenders, while restructuring their economy at the IMF's discretion: these were the famous conditionalities, detailed in the Structural Adjustment Programmes. The IMF and its ultra-liberal experts took control of the borrowing countries' economic policies. A new form of colonisation was thus instituted. It was not even necessary to establish an administrative or military presence; the debt alone maintained this new form of submission.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-175) International politics play an important role in IMF decision making. The clout of member states is roughly proportional to its contribution to IMF finances. The United States has the greatest number of votes and therefore wields the most influence. Domestic politics often come into play, with politicians in developing countries using conditionality to gain leverage over the opposition to influence policy.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-IMF:_Politics_of_Conditional_Lending-176)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-177) Academic Jeremy Garlick cites IMF loans to South Korea during the [1997 Asian financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Asian_financial_crisis "1997 Asian financial crisis") as widely perceived by the South Korean public as a debt-trap.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-:13-178):89 Garlick writes that the public was generally bitter about submitting to the conditions imposed by the IMF, which required South Korea to radically restructure its economy and consult with the IMF before making economic decisions until the debt was repaid.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-:13-178):89 In 2016, the IMF's research department published a report titled "Neoliberalism: Oversold?" which, while praising some aspects of the "[neoliberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoliberal "Neoliberal") agenda", claims that the organisation has been "overselling" fiscal [austerity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austerity "Austerity") policies and financial deregulation, which they claim has exacerbated both financial crises and [economic inequality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_inequality "Economic inequality") around the world.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-179)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-180)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-181) In 2020 and 2021, Oxfam criticized the IMF for forcing tough austerity measures on many low income countries during the COVID-19 pandemic, despite forcing cuts to healthcare spending, would hamper the recipient's response to the pandemic.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-182)[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-183) ### Support of dictatorships [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=International_Monetary_Fund&action=edit&section=35 "Edit section: Support of dictatorships")] The role of the [Bretton Woods institutions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bretton_Woods_system "Bretton Woods system") has been controversial since the late [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), because of claims that the IMF policy makers supported [military dictatorships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_dictatorship "Military dictatorship") friendly to American and European corporations, but also other [anti-communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-communist "Anti-communist") and [communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist "Communist") regimes, such as the [Socialist Republic of Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Republic_of_Romania "Socialist Republic of Romania"). An example of IMF's support for a dictatorship was its ongoing support for [Mobutu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobutu "Mobutu")'s rule in [Zaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaire "Zaire"), although its own envoy Erwin Blumenthal provided a sobering report about the entrenched corruption and embezzlement and the inability of the country to pay back any loans.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-dvr-184) In 2021, the IMF approved a US$1 billion loan to the [autocratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autocratic "Autocratic") Uganda despite protests from Ugandans in Washington, London and South Africa.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-185)[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-186) Critics also claim that the IMF is generally apathetic or hostile to democracy, human rights, and [labour rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labour_rights "Labour rights"). The controversy has helped spark the [anti-globalization movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-globalization_movement "Anti-globalization movement"). Arguments in favour of the IMF supporting dictatorships is the claim that [economic stability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_stability "Economic stability") is a precursor to democracy. A 2017 study found no evidence of IMF lending programs undermining democracy in borrowing countries,[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-:0-187) it found "evidence for modest but definitively positive conditional differences in the democracy scores of participating and non-participating countries".[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-:0-187) A 2020 study found the reverse causality with [democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democracy "Democracy") as a precursor to economic stability.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-j902-188) Critics highlight various examples in which democratised countries fell after receiving IMF loans.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-cadtm-189) Party-based autocracies and democracies can face similar incentives when considering agreements with IMF, in contrast to personalist and military regimes.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-q511-190) ### Impact on access to food [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=International_Monetary_Fund&action=edit&section=36 "Edit section: Impact on access to food")] A number of [civil society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_society "Civil society") organisations[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-191) have criticised the IMF's policies for their impact on access to food, particularly in developing countries. In October 2008, former United States president [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") delivered a speech to the United Nations on [World Food Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Food_Day "World Food Day"), criticising the World Bank and IMF for their policies on food and agriculture: > We need the World Bank, the IMF, all the big foundations, and all the governments to admit that, for 30 years, we all blew it, including me when I was president. We were wrong to believe that food was like some other product in international trade, and we all have to go back to a more responsible and [sustainable form of agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainable_agriculture "Sustainable agriculture"). —Former U.S. president Bill Clinton, Speech at United Nations World Food Day, October 16, 2008[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-192) The [FPIF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FPIF?action=edit&redlink=1 "FPIF (page does not exist)") remarked that there is a recurring pattern: "the destabilization of peasant producers by a one-two punch of IMF-[World Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank "World Bank") structural adjustment programs that gutted government investment in the countryside followed by the massive influx of subsidized U.S. and European Union agricultural imports after the [WTO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTO "WTO")'s Agreement on Agriculture pried open markets."[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-Foreign_Policy_In_Focus_2008-193) ### Impact on public health [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=International_Monetary_Fund&action=edit&section=37 "Edit section: Impact on public health")] The structural adjustments programs (SAPs) demanded by IMF conditionality contribute to the weakening of public health services in a number of ways. Cuts in funding to public health services prompted by IMF SAPs contribute to poorer working conditions in the sector, causing repercussions for health service quality and availability.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-194) This has been shown to negatively impact vaccination rates, increase exposure to conditions with risk-factors like disability and death, and higher prevalence of tuberculosis.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-195) A 2009 study concluded that the strict conditions resulted in thousands of deaths in Eastern Europe by [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis "Tuberculosis") as [public health care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_health_care "Public health care") had to be weakened. In the 21 countries to which the IMF had given loans, [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis "Tuberculosis") deaths rose by 16.6%.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-196) A 2017 systematic review on studies conducted on the impact that [structural adjustment programs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_adjustment "Structural adjustment") have on child and maternal health found that these programs have a detrimental effect on maternal and child health among other adverse effects.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-197) Structural adjustment programs are considered a form of neo-colonialism by some academics due to their intensification of healthcare access inequality, and their promotion of external intervention and aid to meet health needs in developing countries.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-198) ### Scandals [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=International_Monetary_Fund&action=edit&section=38 "Edit section: Scandals")] Managing Director Lagarde (2011–2019) was convicted of giving preferential treatment to businessman-turned-politician [Bernard Tapie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Tapie "Bernard Tapie") as he pursued a legal challenge against the French government. At the time, Lagarde was the French economic minister.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-199) Within hours of her conviction, in which she escaped any punishment, the fund's 24-member executive board put to rest any speculation that she might have to resign, praising her "outstanding leadership" and the "wide respect" she commands around the world.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-200) Former IMF Managing Director [Rodrigo Rato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Rato "Rodrigo Rato") was arrested in 2015 for alleged [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud"), [embezzlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embezzlement "Embezzlement") and [money laundering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money_laundering "Money laundering").[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-201)[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-BBC_News_16_April_2015-202) In 2017, the [Audiencia Nacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audiencia_Nacional "Audiencia Nacional") found Rato guilty of embezzlement and sentenced him to 4+1⁄2 years' imprisonment.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-203) In 2018, the sentence was confirmed by the [Supreme Court of Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Spain "Supreme Court of Spain").[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-204) ### Reform [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=International_Monetary_Fund&action=edit&section=39 "Edit section: Reform")] #### Function and policies [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=International_Monetary_Fund&action=edit&section=40 "Edit section: Function and policies")] The IMF is only one of many [international organisations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_organisations "International organisations"), and it is a generalist institution that deals only with macroeconomic issues; its core areas of concern in [developing countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developing_countries "Developing countries") are very narrow. One proposed reform is a movement towards close partnership with other specialist agencies such as [UNICEF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF"), the [Food and Agriculture Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_and_Agriculture_Organization "Food and Agriculture Organization") (FAO), and the [United Nations Development Programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Development_Programme "United Nations Development Programme") (UNDP).[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-The_End_of_Poverty-169) [Jeffrey Sachs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Sachs "Jeffrey Sachs") argues in _[The End of Poverty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_End\_of\_Poverty "The End of Poverty")_ that the IMF and the World Bank have "the brightest economists and the lead in advising poor countries on how to break out of poverty, but the problem is development economics".[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-The_End_of_Poverty-169)[Development economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Development_economics "Development economics") needs the reform, not the IMF. He also notes that IMF loan conditions should be paired with other reforms—e.g., trade reform in [developed nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developed_nations "Developed nations"), [debt cancellation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debt_cancellation "Debt cancellation"), and increased financial assistance for investments in [basic infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrastructure "Infrastructure").[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-The_End_of_Poverty-169) IMF loan conditions cannot stand alone and produce change; they need to be partnered with other reforms or other conditions as applicable.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-Lipscy_2015-11) #### U.S. influence and voting reform [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=International_Monetary_Fund&action=edit&section=41 "Edit section: U.S. influence and voting reform")] The scholarly consensus is that IMF decision-making is not simply technocratic, but also guided by political and economic concerns.[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-Breen_2013_13-205) The United States is the IMF's most powerful member, and its influence reaches even into decision-making concerning individual loan agreements.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-Oatley&Yackee_2004-206) The U.S. has historically been openly opposed to losing what Treasury Secretary [Jacob Lew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Lew "Jacob Lew") described in 2015 as its "leadership role" at the IMF, and the U.S.' "ability to shape international norms and practices".[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-Donnan_Dyer_FT-207) Emerging markets were not well-represented for most of the IMF's history: Despite being the most populous country, China's vote share was the sixth largest; Brazil's vote share was smaller than Belgium's.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-208) Reforms to give more powers to emerging economies were agreed by the [G20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G-20_major_economies "G-20 major economies") in 2010. The reforms could not pass, however, until they were ratified by the [United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress"),[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-nyt-20140325-209)[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-reuters-20140407-210)[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-reuters-20140409-211) since 85% of the Fund's voting power was required for the reforms to take effect,[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-IMF_2010_acceptance-212) and the Americans held more than 16% of voting power at the time.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-IMF_members-2) After repeated criticism,[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-213)[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-Bberg_veto-214) the U.S. finally ratified the voting reforms at the end of 2015.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-215) The [OECD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OECD "OECD") countries maintained their overwhelming majority of voting share, and the U.S. in particular retained its share at over 16%.[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-216) The criticism of the American- and European-dominated IMF has led to what some consider "disenfranchising the world" from the governance of the IMF. [Raúl Prebisch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ra%C3%BAl_Prebisch "Raúl Prebisch"), the founding secretary-general of the [UN Conference on Trade and Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Conference_on_Trade_and_Development "UN Conference on Trade and Development") (UNCTAD), wrote that one of "the conspicuous deficiencies of the general economic theory, from the point of view of the periphery, is its false sense of universality".[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund#cite_note-217) ### Alternatives
